neighbours.label: Biomedical/lab specimen-analysis context: tokens inside clinical or laboratory research text about cells, tissue, samples, spectroscopy and diagnosis (the model is setting up a specimen or measurement noun), weakly spread over health text

The team applied infrared spectroscopy to each blood sample before comparing the readings across all forty patients.

A pathologist reviewed the slides and wrote a report describing the abnormal cells found in the patient's liver.

Methods: we reviewed the clinicopathological records of 120 children and graded the skin findings seen on examination.
Heat from the device is meant to damage fat cells beneath the skin, which the body then clears away over several weeks.
After surgery, the surgeon sent the removed growth to the lab so that doctors could confirm the diagnosis from the specimen.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Top negative activations land on tokens inside lab/biomedical text (spectro-, cells, the sample, diagnosis) and census shows 65% of diseases fire it; but strong band samples are scattered (turtles 'them', recipe 'bowl'), so only a broad biomedical-specimen context is supported. Note the + pole is the tissue/pathology-sample feature and this pole is its reversed, weaker side.
